RotarySpeaker.description:
The Rotary Speaker block (Rotary A + Rotary B).

Balance is a centred value (`0x40` = R=H — see [`balance_label`]); Stereo/Mono is typed. Speed / Acceleration / Transition stay raw `0..=127` indices: the manual documents only their rpm/ratio range + default (exposed via [`ROTARY_SPECS`]), and the device's per-step curve isn't published or derivable (Rotary A and B use different byte→rpm mappings), so no per-byte conversion is provided. Transition is itself a raw `0..=127` value.

a_balance.description: Rotary A balance (horn vs rotor), raw 0..=127 (R63>H .. R=H .. R<H63).

a_horn_fast.description: Rotary A horn fast speed index (209.4–817.6 rpm).

a_horn_slow.description: Rotary A horn slow speed index (23.0–89.6 rpm).

a_rotor_fast.description: Rotary A rotor fast speed index (189.3–736.8 rpm).

a_rotor_slow.description: Rotary A rotor slow speed index (22.7–88.3 rpm).

a_stereo_mono.description: Rotary A output: stereo or mono.

b_horn_fast.description: Rotary B horn fast speed index (161.5–2382 rpm).

b_horn_slow.description: Rotary B horn slow speed index (2.5–159.0 rpm).

b_rotor_fast.description: Rotary B rotor fast speed index (161.5–2382 rpm).

b_rotor_slow.description: Rotary B rotor slow speed index (2.5–159.0 rpm).

b_stereo_mono.description: Rotary B output: stereo or mono.

ZoneTransmit.description:
Which "snapshot" MIDI messages the Zone sends when its Live Set is loaded.

The byte at Zone offset `0x0C` is a bitmask. Bits 0–3 are named in the CK Owner's Manual; bit 4 sits inside the manual's documented `0x00..=0x1F` range without a published meaning. Any higher bits a device emits (defensive) are kept verbatim in `reserved_bits` so the block round-trips byte-exact.

reserved_bits.description: Bits 4..=7 captured verbatim — bit 4 falls inside the manual's documented `0x1F` range but isn't named; higher bits aren't expected but are preserved defensively.

ZoneTransmitControllers.description:
Which live controllers the Zone forwards to its transmit channel.

Byte at Zone offset `0x0D`. Bits 0–3 are documented; bits 4–5 fall inside the manual's `0x00..=0x3F` documented range without published meaning; higher bits are unexpected but preserved.

reserved_bits.description: Bits 4..=7 captured verbatim — bits 4 and 5 sit inside the manual's `0x3F` documented range without a published meaning.
